The main takeaway from our work is that

a careful choice of model formulation and algorithmic techniques can significantly improve the performance of stochastic integer programming algorithms, even when the model is highly complex and the solution space is very large.

, in order to make a L-shaped algorithm for a stochastic integer programming model converge quickly, the master problem must be strengthened with additional valid inequalities and the subproblem must generate a large number of optimality (or feasibility) cuts.

a simple, intuitive approach to modeling stochastic SONET ring design problems can be made computationally effective by incorporating some of the modeling techniques developed for stochastic integer programming.
